exposure: maternal serum total bile acid levels
cohort: 751 pregnant women with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy at 30-32 weeks of gestation
finding: Higher maternal serum total bile acid levels were positively correlated with twin pregnancy and meconium stained amniotic fluid, and infants of mothers with severe intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy were more likely to have food allergies at 6 months.
